stem: Arrange P, Q, R and S to form a coherent five-sentence paragraph. The first and last sentences are fixed. In the mid-nineteenth century, irregularities in Uranus's orbit led astronomers to suspect an unseen planet. P: Initial observers dismissed the suggestion because the deviations were slight, Q: but two mathematicians used them to calculate the position of a possible planet. R: Their calculation, however, did not itself establish the body's existence. S: Observers then searched the indicated region and found a planet close to the predicted position. Neptune's discovery became a celebrated demonstration of how theory can guide observation. Which sequence is correct?

verdicts.working: P–Q form a contrast: observers dismissed the suggestion, but mathematicians used the deviations to calculate a position. R qualifies the calculation; S gives the search and discovery.
